input.question: How is currency/money in banks and other financial institutions safe-guarded from computer-based attacks?
input.ground_truth: Insane amounts of backups. The record keeping is highly regulated and by law the banks/financial institutions must follow the rules of having the information secured, AND backed up in a number of ways. Worst case scenario, they would have to stop all transactions and fix their databases. Source: I build these systems.

So, the bank puts the treasure chest inside a super strong, locked room. The lock is very special—it changes every time you try to open it, and only the right key (which is a secret password and some other secret things) can open it.

Also, the bank has friendly robots (these are like security programs) that watch the doors all the time. If a pirate tries to break in, the robots shout for help and lock everything down.

And the bank keeps making the locks and robots even better, so the pirates can’t trick them.

That’s how the bank keeps the gold (money) safe from computer pirates!
